item.title: Toyama Bay: Where the Northern Alps Meet the Sea — Guide
item.description: Toyama Bay is renowned for its dramatic geography, one of the few places in the world where mountains rising above 3,000 metres, the Northern Japan Alps, are visible directly across open water from the coastline, creating a striking contrast between sea and high peaks. The bay is also known for a rare spring mirage phenomenon, when atmospheric conditions bend light to distort the appearance of the far shore, and its unusually steep underwater topography feeds some of Japan’s richest coastal fishing grounds, source of specialties like shiro-ebi and hotaru-ika.
